title: MCP tool risk manifest, version 1 (DRAFT)
description: Per-tool risk of an MCP server's tool surface, with the evidence behind each verdict and the contract it was derived from. Shared by mcpward and KyttoMCP. Consumers MUST ignore properties they do not understand.

manifestVersion.description: Major version of this format. A consumer that sees a higher major version than it supports MUST NOT trust any verdict in the file and SHOULD treat every tool as unknown.

generator.description: The tool that wrote this file.

server.description: What the server said about itself. Self-reported, informational only.

^x-[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$.description: Generator-specific extension. Other consumers ignore it.

canonicalization.description: How each tool's contractHash was computed. Two manifests describe the same contract only if id, version and algorithm match AND the hashes match.

version.description: Version of the canonicalization rules in the spec document. Bumped whenever the rules change.

fields.description: The tool fields that went into the hash, in the canonical object. Fixed per rules version; listed so a consumer can see it without reading the spec.

effect.description: What calling the tool can do to state. 'unknown' is the default and the fail-safe: a consumer MUST NOT treat it as read-only.

openWorld.description: Whether the tool can reach entities outside the server's own domain (web, email, third-party APIs). Orthogonal to effect: a web search is read-only AND open-world.

source.description: annotation: declared by the server (self-reported, unverified). heuristic: derived by the generator from names, descriptions or schema. override: set by a person.

indicates.description: What this piece of evidence points to. A piece of evidence may speak to effect, openWorld, or both.

rule.description: Stable id of the heuristic, namespaced by generator, e.g. 'mcpward/name-verb'.

by.description: Who made the override. Free text; may be omitted for privacy.

verdict.description: The generator's resolved verdict. 'basis' names the evidence source that decided it, so a consumer can choose to distrust, for example, verdicts based only on annotations.

argument.description: OPEN QUESTION: per-argument risk, for tools that are only risky when given a certain input (a path, a URL, free-form context).

contractHash.description: Hash of this tool's canonical contract, per the file's canonicalization block.

evidence.description: Every signal considered, including ones the verdict overrode. Empty array means no evidence; the verdict must then be unknown with basis none.
